scale_decision.source_of_measurement: Two independent measurements, both used: (1) data/results/2026-09-17-t32-replay-engine/result.json -- 50 OD pairs, single config, 138.1s (run A) = 2.76s/call; (2) this task's own pre-run smoke test -- 3 OD pairs x 6 configs = 18 calls, 55.2s = 3.07s/call, used as the more conservative figure below. This CLI invocation cost is dominated by per-process graph load (471,240 edges) + ALT-landmark rebuild, not by the search itself (expected 10-40ms per CLAUDE.md); the CLI has no batch/warm-process mode, a real harness-level inefficiency out of this task's scope to fix (packages/pulse_router is off-limits per this task's constraints).
scale_decision.honest_scale_statement: N=1000 (docs/EVALUATION.md's target) x 6 configs x a multi-point Pareto sweep would cost several hours of pure CLI subprocess time at this measured per-call cost, with no batching mechanism available. Scaled down to N_main=100 per main config and N_sweep=25 per Pareto grid point (5x3=15 points), stated here explicitly rather than silently under-running, per this task's instruction.

event_split.honest_limitation: T3.1's corpus (data/corpus/2026-09-17/) carries exactly one degenerate proxy timestamp for all 6,132 observations (2015-12-02T00:00:00Z, MANIFEST.md limitation 1) -- there is no second event or monsoon episode to hold out. This is a genuine single-fold application of a correctly-implemented general split, not a random split and not a fabricated multi-event split. A true train/held-out-event evaluation is not currently possible with this corpus.
